prompt: Build a highly detailed rotating space station orbiting Earth: a large torus habitat ring with spokes, a central hub with docking ports and engines, solar array wings, trusses, a robotic arm, antennas and a docked shuttle. Add panel seams, greebles and running lights, and an interior garden deck with windows. Texture it with realistic metals, glass and emissives. Animate the ring rotating and the shuttle docking. Place 10 cinematic cameras like a Hollywood commercial (wide establishing shots, close detail passes, an interior reveal, a sunrise over Earth) and render a 50-second 4K video.

summary: Gemini 4 Argon autonomously authored 3D models, materials, animation, and multi-camera cinematography for a space station scene rendered in Mixar/Cycles.

post.originalText:
An AI agent built this entire space station.

Modeling, materials, animation, cameras: all done by Gemini 4 Argon inside Mixar (an AI-native Blender fork). 

I didn't touch the mouse once.

It's not an AI video. It's real 3D geometry, rendered in 4K.

Prompt and clay breakdown in the replies 👇

sourceMaterials.text: @catmanyau It worked from the existing scene. The agent kept editing the same scene across passes, adding the camera setup and animation on top of the existing geometry and materials.
sourceMaterials.author: _satyam_ai

sourceMaterials.text: @mindofstephen Haha, nice observation. This is more of a visual exploration than an engineering-ready design. The goal here was to see how far an AI agent could go in building a complete 3D scene autonomously.
sourceMaterials.author: _satyam_ai

sourceMaterials.text: @catmanyau I have the timelapse for the first 30–40 minutes, but unfortunately, it doesn’t cover the entire build because the recording stopped midway.
sourceMaterials.author: _satyam_ai

sourceMaterials.text: @catmanyau The agent was editing a shared scene. It generated the geometry and materials in the first pass. Then I asked it to add more geometric detail and refine the materials. Finally, I asked it to handle camera placement and animation.
sourceMaterials.author: _satyam_ai

sourceMaterials.text: @catmanyau Exactly. The video is just the final render. The actual 3D scene, geometry, materials, animation, and cameras were all created by the agents.
sourceMaterials.author: _satyam_ai

The prompt I started with:

"Build a highly detailed rotating space station orbiting Earth: a large torus habitat ring with spokes, a central hub with docking ports and engines, solar array wings, trusses, a robotic arm, antennas and a docked shuttle. Add panel seams, greebles and running lights, and an interior garden deck with windows. Texture it with realistic metals, glass and emissives. Animate the ring rotating and the shuttle docking. Place 10 cinematic cameras like a Hollywood commercial (wide establishing shots, close detail passes, an interior reveal, a sunrise over Earth) and render a 50-second 4K video."

After that it was a few rounds of direction: shot order, sharpening and a Cycles render.
